records.name: Chicagon / Chicaugon Falls
records.title: State-owned waterfall; no proven continuous public approach
records.summary: Michigan DNR land records put Chicagon Falls on a dedicated 47.8-acre state forest parcel. An official forest-management report for the surrounding Chicagon Creek compartment warns that private landowners control almost all vehicle access to that compartment. County tourism guides describe a signed Raymer/Dave's Camp trail but report washouts and passing private camps. None of this establishes today's lawful parking or a continuous public trail to the waterfall.
records.guidance: The waterfall's state parcel is verified, but do NOT navigate to the GIS point, cross private camps or assume Raymer/Dave's Camp Road is passable and public to its end. A signed, legal lot-to-view path needs verification before a visitor guide can be indexed.
records.locationNotes: Michigan GIS #12 at 46.134032,-88.452985 agrees broadly with other geographic catalogs around 46.1336,-88.4535; a separate tourism listing reports 46.1089,-88.4903, a materially different location. The latter must not be substituted as parking or falls position.
records.reviewLimitations: 2019/2020-era DNR compartment 12139 concerns the surrounding Chicagon Creek forest area, not a survey or specific trail deed for falls #12. County road commission's 2018 seasonal-restriction list includes Long Lake Road but does not show Raymer/Dave's Camp in that list; absence proves neither private ownership nor closure. State MGF geographic road-name data near the falls identifies Long Lake Road but not a named Raymer segment, which also is not a legal road determination. Exact right-of-way, parking and current passability remain unverified.
records.nextEvidence: Obtain an authoritative legal public right-of-way or DNR access map from Long Lake Road through Raymer/Dave's Camp to the state parcel, including permission at private camps, a designated turnout and footpath; until then no vehicle waypoint or public trail line.

records.name: Gabbro / Baker's Falls
records.title: Gabbro/Baker's: City describes two approaches, land boundary pending
records.summary: The City of Bessemer identifies Gabbro/Baker's Falls and describes two approaches near the Blackjack Ski Hill bridge and upper hillside. An independent hiking account describes an informal marked trail, while regional tourism describes a gas/powerline clearing. These are distinct visitor proposals; a legal public parking site and continuous foot access through the ski-hill/utility corridor have not been independently established.
records.guidance: Use this research point to plan verification, not to drive to the waterfall GPS or follow an unsourced pipeline shortcut. A future guide requires a mapped legal parking approach and designated public viewing trail, with rough sections and seasonal conditions made explicit.
records.locationNotes: Michigan state GIS #38 marks the natural Black River falls; no separately certified visitor lot or full legal walking line has been established.
records.reviewLimitations: The city recommendation confirms a named visitor attraction, but is not a route survey, public easement or current vehicle road status. Gogebic County's official parcel viewer cautions against legal/title use, and the falls GIS point does not lie in a returned MI DNR LOTS managed parcel at the sampled point. No DNR layer hit is not private-property proof.
records.nextEvidence: Determine jurisdiction/owner of the bridge turnout and upper service road, establish ski-resort permission or public trail easement and official safe parking, then distinguish publicly authorized upper and lower views. Avoid the unverified utility-corridor shortcut.

records.name: Sturgeon Falls
records.title: Sturgeon Falls: Michigan GIS pin conflicts with verified visitor waterfall
records.summary: Michigan state GIS #45 is 6.74 km south of the Sturgeon Falls location independently documented by the North Country Trail Association (46.64242,-88.69346), Visit Keweenaw (46.6428,-88.6937), and geographic field accounts. The official public visitor guide is based on the corroborated gorge waterfall location, NOT this GIS point.
records.guidance: Do not drive or hike to state GIS #45 expecting the visitor waterfall. Use the separate official Sturgeon River Gorge Wilderness trailhead and NCTA 2025 map. This GIS marker is displayed only in the opt-in research map until spatial identity can be established.
records.reviewLimitations: Same name does not prove the state source maps a different physical falls or an error. Road naming also differs between NCTA 2014 FR2276 and 2025 FR2270 descriptions, so use current signed Forest Service roads.
records.nextEvidence: Verify GIS feature #45 with modern federal hydrography and exact stream location; establish if separate cascade or coordinate error. Never auto-merge by name.

records.name: Tioga Falls
records.title: Tioga Falls: access evidence under review
records.summary: A specialist waterfall field record places Tioga Falls at a Tioga River cascade near a private camp and explicitly describes a signed private-property gate blocking the easier south approach. Suggested river crossings and off-trail alternatives are not verified lawful visitor paths.
records.guidance: Do not tell visitors to pass the gate, cross the river to bypass private land or take the GIS coordinates as a car destination. Keep research-only until an authorized public trailhead, parking and continuous permitted approach exist.
records.reviewLimitations: Third-party historical route description is not a legal parcel survey or 2026 gate status; absence of a public route is not proof that every possible access is legally closed.
records.nextEvidence: Check land boundaries/permissions from owner or authoritative land manager and an independently designated safe public parking and trail route; no informal ford guidance.

records.name: Bonanza Falls / Greenwood Falls
records.title: Township upper-falls park verified; GIS point is outside mapped park
records.summary: Carp Lake Township explicitly lists Greenwoods (Bonanza Falls) as a public park with falls and publishes its map destination. The official map destination and regional upper-river view reference lie within a township-attributed parcel; Michigan's separate natural waterfall GIS #124 location lies outside it on a parcel attributed to a private LLC. The guide covers the short signed park approach to the upper falls only.
records.guidance: Use only the signed township park entrance and short established path from designated parking to the upper river view, then return. Do not drive to the GIS falls point, infer access to all downstream drops, or assume the seasonal park is open today.
records.locationNotes: Township Google Maps published destination 46.8176942,-89.5674561 (NOT verified lot); regional brochure upper-view reference 46.817719,-89.570023 (NOT surveyed viewpoint); state natural falls GIS #124 46.818863,-89.571458 on other attributed parcel. Route is signed, not surveyed or traced on the map.

records.name: Dead River Falls
records.title: Dead River Falls: access evidence under review
records.summary: Marquette Township official approved recreation plan names Dead River Falls in Forestville and confirms a DIFFERENT state-owned Forestville Access Site for boating. Independent Falls River specialist places hiking path beside old power station and parking near outhouse, but current utility ownership, public parking permission, walk past service gate, and posted hiking rule are unverified. State-owned boat access is not automatic hiking access to falls.
records.guidance: Do not recommend utility lot or service road as confirmed public parking; a forest access boat launch is not a falls trailhead.
records.reviewLimitations: Printed tourism map describes the visitor route, not current utility power-station permissions or a surveyed legal parking lot. Variable hike distances from independent guides are not parking-to-falls measurements.
records.nextEvidence: Find authoritative 2026 powerplant operator or land manager statement confirming lawful public use of powerhouse parking, gate-side pedestrian corridor, and designated falls path; do not substitute state boat-launch or NTN trail lot.

records.name: Au Train Falls
records.title: Au Train: two visitor approaches; utility rights need checking
records.summary: Munising visitor sources describe two different Power Dam Road parking areas, one for upper cascades and another for lower falls beyond a gate. The Au Train dam has faced federal safety compliance and license-surrender proceedings, with reported property/operating-right changes in 2025. Those reports do not prove the waterfall area is currently closed or open.
records.guidance: Do not infer permission through utility gates or present a current safe parking/walking route until the dam operator's current access rules and federal project status are verified. Water release conditions can change and are not monitored here.
records.reviewLimitations: Historical tourism directions do not establish 2026 utility landowner permission; reporting on proposed license surrender is not a final current FERC status or an official public closure order.
records.nextEvidence: Check current FERC project docket and dam operator identity, public-access condition at both Power Dam Road parking areas, and gates/posted warnings. Preserve upper and lower falls as separate access experiences.

records.name: Alger Falls
records.title: Alger Falls: no safe parking in city plan
records.summary: Munising's adopted recreation plan says there are no safe parking options at the roadside Alger Falls viewing area by M-28/M-94. Older tourist and hiking accounts mention a turnout, but they do not supersede the city's documented road-safety concern.
records.guidance: Do not stop in travel lanes, walk over the guardrail or use the waterfall GIS point as a parking destination. Safe public parking and pedestrian access require current MDOT confirmation.
records.reviewLimitations: Adopted municipal recreation planning evidence establishes a serious safety concern; it does not establish that all road shoulders are legally closed or that no future improvement has occurred.
records.nextEvidence: Verify current MDOT designated turnout, safe walking/crossing area and whether a legal official view can be reached without stopping on the highway.
